hypothesis: The newly integrated coroutine feature might allocate a task scheduler or extra guest capability on every Core tick even without authored routines.
scope: Source inspection only; no native execution, new profiling or optimization.
findings: Neither current Core gameplay.ts nor stress.ts declares a coroutine catalog.
Catalog.enabled() reads a boolean established at program loading. The compiler selects the existing 16-argument update wrapper once when routineCount is zero.

The host constructs a coroutine Tick, restores its shape, exposes capabilities and uses the expanded callback only when the catalog is enabled. The no-catalog path retains absent coroutine state; Option cloning does not allocate a task map.
This source check does not prove zero overhead or current shipping timing. Ordinary function layout, branches and compiler effects require a matched measurement before making any performance claim.
result: No unnecessary scheduler or coroutine-capability allocation found for Core; no source-grounded optimization from this hypothesis.
prior_results: Existing deadline-check, repeated-start, graph-cache, numeric-view, typed-store and allocation results remain unchanged; no repeat scheduled.
next_trigger: A distinct non-navigation callback subpath with attributable cost evidence, or another relevant runtime change; perform a bounded subagent review when capacity permits. Any candidate needs matched shipping-profile measurements and exact gameplay/audio parity.
